purpose: Provenance for every behavior represented by the disposable mobile contract mock. This is evidence metadata, not production authority.

levels.machine-generated: Extracted from deployed OpenAPI or the running integration guide and checked mechanically.
levels.source-read: Confirmed by strugglebus-agent after reading the deployed release source.
levels.runtime-observed: Observed against the deployed service or a real Android emulator.
levels.assumed: Proposed mobile behavior not yet implemented in StruggleBus; requires future source confirmation.

behaviors.mock: A successful one-time redemption returns one non-empty secret.
Token validation precedes any request-id lookup and only a secret hash is retained; redemption replay is refused.
Credential operations that are idempotent distinguish issued secrets from secretless replay.
Three concurrent streams and a 300-second production lifetime; tests may override lifetime only.
Snapshot never calls catch-up and never advances a consuming cursor.
Authenticated mobile requests coalesce last-use writes within the activity window.
Compact ASCII-escaped JSON, literal heartbeat comments, signed 64-bit sequence IDs, and terminal events without IDs.
Status reports frozen while snapshot, channels, agents, and stream continue returning real monitor data.
Mobile credentials use a distinct principal and credential namespace and cannot authenticate as agents.
An active monitor can view all channels; client filtering does not narrow server authorization.
Credential and availability denial can terminate a stream between messages; freeze no longer terminates or truncates mobile delivery.
The operator password is exchanged once for a returned-once per-device grant; replacement revokes the prior grant and creation is denied while frozen.

evidence: StruggleBus v0.2.22 OpenAPI MobileConfirmationRequest/Response and MobileActionRequest
behaviors.mock: A short-lived confirmation binds one action and target; the action must redeclare the same pair and supply a human audit reason.
Existing grants can activate or clear the global freeze while grant creation remains denied.
The app closes its active stream when backgrounded and resumes from the durable accepted sequence when foregrounded.
Keystore credential state and the accepted sequence survive process termination; a new process resumes without replaying accepted messages.
A stream ending at the real five-minute boundary is classified as routine closure rather than failure.
